Call? Why this works

It's a real thing. It's called rubber ducking.

Why a rubber duck

Saying it out loud is the point.

Rubber ducking means talking through a problem, step by step, to something that won't interrupt or judge. Just articulating it is often enough to see the gaps yourself — no advice required.

So why a stranger instead of an actual duck? Because some of the most honest conversations happen with people who have nothing at stake in your life.

Apollo is

An ear

Control is an illusion. Saying a thought out loud can bring you clarity before you even reach the end of the sentence.

Bias-free

No stake in your life means no agenda to push. If you're stuck between a rock and a hard place, a fair second opinion might help.

Forgetful

I don't know who you are or what you did. Just a forgetful friend who's happy to hear you out, then let it go.

About

Meet Apollo.

By day, I trade global equities — top-10 school, tennis on the weekends. But the thing I'm proudest of is being a 3am friend.

Sometimes you don't need advice, a plan, or a professional. You just need to get it off your chest, without giving context or committing to anything.

So people don't call to prank or waste it. I have a fairly successful career that doesn't need me to do this — I do it because I want to.

I am not. Think of me as someone you met at a bar while grabbing a drink, and a conversation happened. No context needed, no arrangement to commit to.

Yes, like a stranger would. Ask what I think and I'll answer — just know I'll never have the full context. I'm human, and everything I say is my own perspective.

Sure, as long as it's not a crime. I promise I'll hang up if you try that.
